name: Desktop 1.0.24 (macOS, Windows, Linux)
body:
## What's New

### Finishes the random sign-out fix — the app now actually uses its renewed session
1.0.23 fixed the session-renewal races on the server side, but one desktop-side flaw remained — and it turned out to be the root of the "randomly signed out" reports. When the app renewed your session in the background, it saved the new login token to disk **but kept using the old one from memory**. About a minute later the old token expired, every request from the app started failing, and nothing recovered until you restarted the app or your machine slept and woke. This release fixes that at the source:

- **Renewed sessions take effect immediately.** The freshly-stored token is now used the moment it's saved — no restart, no sleep/wake needed. This also makes the automatic sign-in recovery shipped in 1.0.23 actually succeed, since it no longer reads back the same stale token it was trying to replace.
- **Signing out fully clears the session everywhere.** Previously a cleared login could linger in memory; now it's invalidated on the spot, so a known-bad token can never keep being sent.

### No more bouncing to the sign-in screen
The other half of this fix lives on the server and is already live: the app's window navigations are no longer redirected to the sign-in form just because a browser cookie went missing while your actual desktop login was still perfectly valid. Updating to 1.0.24 completes the fix end-to-end.

> If you've been hitting sign-outs in normal use, this update should end them. If anything odd persists after updating, signing out and back in once will give you a clean slate.

|----------|------|
| macOS | `PageSpace.dmg` |
| Windows | `PageSpace.exe` |
| Linux | `PageSpace.AppImage` · `PageSpace.deb` · `PageSpace.rpm` |

name: Desktop 1.0.23 (macOS, Windows, Linux)
body:
## What's New

### Fixes intermittent sign-outs
This release fixes a bug where the desktop app could sign you out unexpectedly — sometimes in bursts — during normal use. Recently-enabled edge session checks on the server surfaced two latent flaws in how the app renews its login in the background:

- **Session hand-off no longer races itself.** When the app renewed your session, the old session was being invalidated the instant the new one was created. In-flight requests still carrying the previous token (notably the 1‑second "active streams" check) would then fail in a burst and knock you out. The old session is now retired with a short grace window so those requests finish cleanly.
- **A token-rotation race no longer wipes your login.** Under concurrent renewals, the app could be handed back an already-retired device token and save it, guaranteeing a sign-out on the next cycle. The app now keeps the good token it already holds and, on a transient rejection, quietly retries once with a fresh token before ever logging you out.

### More stable device identity
The desktop app now derives a **stable device identifier that survives hostname and network (VPN) changes**. Previously the fallback identifier could change when your computer's hostname changed, which the server read as a new, untrusted device and forced a re-login. The identifier is now generated once and reused, and it stays consistent even if saving it to disk temporarily fails.

### Clearer diagnostics
Sign-out events now carry a machine-readable reason end-to-end, so the exact cause of any future logout is visible in the logs instead of being guesswork.

> Most of the server-side half of this fix is already live; updating the desktop app completes it and brings the more-stable device identity. If you're currently stuck in a sign-out loop, signing out and back in once will clear it immediately.

| Linux | `PageSpace.AppImage` · `PageSpace.deb` · `PageSpace.rpm` |

name: Desktop 1.0.22 (macOS, Windows, Linux)
body:
## What's New

### Passkey support across the desktop app
Passkeys now work end-to-end in the desktop app — sign-in, sign-up, and adding a passkey to an existing account from **Settings → Security**. Previously the WebAuthn ceremony ran inside Electron's Chromium, which cannot drive Touch ID or Windows Hello without entitlements we don't ship, so the button silently no-op'd. The ceremony now runs in your system browser and returns via a secure one-time deep link — the same pattern we already use for Google / Apple OAuth.

- **Sign in with Passkey** opens your system browser, prompts for Touch ID / Windows Hello / your security key, and returns you to the app when the exchange completes.
- **Create account with Passkey** uses the same handoff flow for new registrations.
- **Add Passkey from account settings** is new in this release: authenticated desktop users can now attach a new passkey to their existing account. The ceremony carries a short-lived, one-time registration handoff token (300s TTL, atomic consume, never in URL logs) so the system browser can authorise the registration without needing your PageSpace session cookie.

### OS authenticator is now the default for new passkeys
New passkey registrations default to your local platform authenticator (Touch ID on macOS, Windows Hello on Windows) via WebAuthn Level 3 `hints: ['client-device']`. You can still register a cross-device passkey or security key from the browser's native picker — portability is preserved, but the default is the faster local path.

### Also in this release
- **Desktop OAuth callback fix** — the service worker no longer intercepts top-level navigations, restoring Google / Apple OAuth sign-in on desktop in edge cases where the return URL was being hijacked.
- **Clearer error when the desktop IPC bridge is missing** — if your desktop app is too old to support the new passkey handoff, sign-in now shows an explicit "please update the app" toast instead of failing silently.
- **Hardened desktop passkey path** — removes a legacy raw-token branch, bounds `deviceName`, and tightens the audit trail on the passkey authenticate endpoint.
- **Backend: SIEM + audit infrastructure** — unified audit pipeline across 200+ API routes, dual-source delivery receipts, chain verification, and PII scrubbing across auth logs. Invisible to desktop users but strengthens the server your app connects to.

## Downloads

| Platform | File |
|----------|------|
| macOS | `PageSpace.dmg` |
| Windows | `PageSpace.exe` |
| Linux | `PageSpace.AppImage` / `.deb` / `.rpm` |

## Upgrading

If you were briefly on the unpublished `desktop-v1.0.21` hot-fix build earlier today, update to `1.0.22` — it includes the full passkey add-from-settings flow that `1.0.21` was missing. `1.0.21` has been withdrawn.

name: Desktop 1.0.20 (macOS, Windows, Linux)
body:
## What's New

### Desktop Auth Overhaul
All authentication methods now work properly in the desktop app — passkeys, magic links, Google/Apple OAuth, and Google One-Tap. Previously only Google/Apple OAuth had desktop-specific token handling; other methods relied on Set-Cookie headers which don't persist in Electron. OAuth sign-in now opens in your system browser with a waiting dialog in the app.

### Also in this release
- **Local model timeout fix** — increased fetch proxy timeouts (30s to 2min activity, 5min overall) so local models like LM Studio and Ollama have time to load before the connection drops
- **Session stability** — fixed an issue where users could be logged out after ~5 minutes
- **Security hardening** — SSRF cloud metadata blocklist, PKCE for Google OAuth, HMAC-verified OAuth state, ReDoS-safe URL validation

name: Desktop 1.0.19 (macOS, Windows, Linux)
body:
## What's New

### Local AI Provider Bridge
PageSpace Desktop can now connect directly to local AI providers running on your machine — Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and any OpenAI-compatible local server. The desktop app proxies requests through Electron's main process, bypassing browser CORS restrictions that previously blocked local connections. Configure your local provider URL in Settings → AI Providers and start chatting with your own models.

### Also in this release
- **Voice mode** — talk to AI with desktop microphone permissions
- **AI SDK v5 compatibility** — updated parameter handling for latest AI SDK
- **Architecture improvements** — desktop main process refactored into focused modules for better maintainability

name: Desktop 1.0.9 (macOS, Linux, Windows)
body:
**PageSpace Desktop v1.0.9 Release Notes**

  **What's New**

  Improved WebSocket Connection Reliability

  This release includes a complete overhaul of how the desktop app authenticates with the PageSpace server, resulting in more stable and reliable connections.

  **Key improvements:**

  - More reliable connections — Eliminated timing-related authentication failures that could occur with the previous JWT-based system
  - Faster reconnection — Simplified authentication flow means quicker reconnects after network interruptions
  - Better error feedback — The app now provides clearer feedback when authentication issues occur, distinguishing between expired sessions and rate limiting

  **Enhanced Security**

  - Session expiration enforcement — WebSocket connections now properly respect session timeouts, ensuring connections are closed when your session expires
  - Instant session revocation — Changing your password or logging out now immediately invalidates all desktop connections

  **Technical Details**

  - Migrated WebSocket authentication from JWT challenge-response to opaque session tokens
  - Added rate limiting protection for token requests (10 requests/minute)
  - Session tokens expire after 1 hour, requiring re-authentication

name: Desktop 1.0.11 (Mac OS, Linux, Windows)
body:
Desktop Release Notes
Bug Fix: MCP Tools Now Available Immediately
Fixed: MCP tools that were configured and enabled would sometimes not appear on first load, requiring users to wait or refresh before they could use their MCP integrations with the AI assistant.

What changed: The desktop app now properly waits until MCP server tools are fully loaded before showing them as available. Previously, there was a brief window where the server would report as "running" but the tools hadn't finished loading yet, causing them to appear empty.

Impact: MCP tools will now reliably appear in the AI chat input as soon as you open the app - no more missing tools on first render or needing to toggle the MCP setting to get them to show up.

name: Desktop 1.0.10 (Mac OS)
body:
**Summary**
Fix MCP tools failing with "Desktop app not connected" error
Extract auth storage functions to shared auth-storage.ts module
WSClient now uses loadAuthSession() from secure storage (same as Socket.IO)
Problem
WSClient was reading JWT from browser cookies, which may not exist due to:

**Domain mismatch**
httpOnly flags
Timing issues on startup
This was technical debt - WSClient was created before secure storage existed (Oct 2025) and was never updated when the Auth Flow Overhaul added loadAuthSession() (Nov 2025).

**Solution**
Use the same token source as Socket.IO - Electron secure storage via loadAuthSession().

name: Desktop 1.0.4 (macOS, Linux, Windows)
body:
## 🚀 Local MCP Server Support

PageSpace Desktop now supports **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** servers, allowing you to extend your AI assistants with powerful local tools - just like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Roo Code. This is PageSpace's first desktop-exclusive feature, bringing the full MCP ecosystem to your workflows.

### What This Means for You

MCP servers give your AI assistants access to local resources and capabilities. Want your AI to read files from your computer, interact with GitHub repositories, or send Slack messages? Now it can. You have full control over which servers run and what permissions they have.

### Key Features

- **Full MCP Server Management** - Add, configure, start, stop, and monitor MCP servers through an intuitive UI in Settings > Local MCP Servers
- **Claude Desktop Compatible** - Use the same configuration format as Claude Desktop. Copy-paste your existing configs or share new ones between apps
- **AI Chat Integration** - MCP tools are immediately available in your AI conversations. No additional setup required once servers are running
- **Cross-Platform** - Works on macOS, Windows, and Linux with automatic command resolution

### Getting Started

1. Open **Settings > Local MCP Servers** (desktop app only)
2. Go to the Configuration tab to edit your MCP config
3. Add your first server - for example, filesystem access:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "filesystem": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/folder"],
      "autoStart": true
    }
  }
}
```
4. Start the server and verify it shows "Running" status
5. Open any AI chat - MCP tools are now available to your assistant

**Note**: Requires Node.js/npx installed on your system to run most MCP servers.

### Documentation

- Architecture details: `/docs/3.0-guides-and-tools/desktop-local-mcp-architecture.md`

We're excited to release the latest version of PageSpace Desktop with important UI improvements and better offline handling!

## 🎉 What's New

### Windows

2. Click "Run anyway" to proceed with installation

We plan to add code signing for Windows in a future release.

The app is fully signed and notarized by Apple. You should not see any security warnings.

For AppImage: Make the file executable (`chmod +x PageSpace.AppImage`) and run it. No installation required.

The in-app auto-updater will notify you of future releases automatically. Make sure to download the `latest-*.yml` file corresponding to your platform if you're distributing the app.

- Fixed offline state showing blank screen instead of error message

name: Desktop 1.0.0 (Mac OS)
body:
# PageSpace Desktop Mac OS 1.0.0

**First Official Desktop Release** - Native desktop application for PageSpace

## What's New

### Native Desktop Experience
- **System Integration**: Native desktop app with system tray support
- **Minimize to Tray**: Keep PageSpace running in the background
- **Deep Linking**: Support for `pagespace://` URLs
- **Window State**: Remembers your window size and position

### Automatic Updates (macOS)
- **Auto-updates**: Automatically checks for updates every 4 hours
- **Manual Check**: Check for updates anytime via Help → Check for Updates
- **Smart Installation**: Downloads in background, prompts when ready to install
- **Seamless Updates**: Update installs automatically on app quit

## How It Works

The desktop app connects to your PageSpace cloud instance at [www.pagespace.ai](https://www.pagespace.ai), providing a native experience with better system integration than using a web browser.

## Installation

**macOS**:
1. Download and open the DMG file
2. Drag PageSpace to Applications folder
3. Launch from Applications or Spotlight

## Feedback

Report issues or request features at: https://github.com/2witstudios/PageSpace/issues
